prompt: Explain climate-smart agriculture and how farmers adapt.
hook: Farming has to change with the weather.

card.oneLiner: Climate-smart agriculture combines better seeds, water and soil practices to keep yields stable as the climate changes.
keyPoints: Stress-tolerant crop varieties cope with heat and drought.
Efficient irrigation stretches limited water.
Soil health and diversification reduce risk.
Climate information services help timing decisions.

framework.name: Indian Council of Agricultural Research
framework.gloss: Research on crops tolerant to heat, drought and pests.

framework.name: National Action Plan on Climate Change

whatYouCanDo: Use soil and water tests to guide inputs.
Diversify crops and income to spread risk.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. Suitable practices vary by region and soil.

sources.title: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

prompt: Explain soil health and why it matters for climate and food.
hook: Soil is alive, and it stores carbon.

card.oneLiner: Healthy soil holds water and carbon and supports crops, while degraded soil releases carbon and lowers yields.
keyPoints: Organic matter feeds soil life and stores carbon.
Better soil holds more water, helping in dry spells.
Erosion and overuse strip nutrients and carbon.
Soil testing guides balanced fertiliser use.

framework.name: Soil Health Card scheme
framework.gloss: Programme providing soil nutrient status to farmers.

framework.name: FAO
framework.gloss: Global guidance on sustainable soil management.

whatYouCanDo: Add organic matter and reduce unnecessary fertiliser.
Avoid burning residue that destroys soil life.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. Recommendations depend on soil type and crop.

prompt: Explain millets and why they are promoted as climate-resilient crops.

card.oneLiner: Millets need less water and tolerate heat better than many cereals, and they are promoted for both nutrition and climate resilience.
keyPoints: They grow on marginal land with little irrigation.
They are nutritious and gluten-free.
A global year highlighted millets in 2023.
Market and processing support affects adoption.

framework.name: FAO
framework.gloss: Global recognition of millets' climate and nutrition value.

framework.name: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
framework.gloss: National support for millet production and markets.

whatYouCanDo: Include millets in meals and school menus.
Support local millet farmers and processors.
Learn the different millet varieties grown locally.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. Agronomic suitability varies by region.

prompt: Explain food loss and waste and its climate cost.

card.oneLiner: A large share of food is lost or wasted, and it accounts for a significant slice of greenhouse gases, so reducing waste is climate action.
keyPoints: Loss happens on farms and in supply chains; waste happens at homes and shops.
Wasted food wastes the land, water and energy used to grow it.
Rotten food in landfills releases methane.
Better storage, cold chains and behaviour all reduce loss.

framework.name: FAO
framework.gloss: Global assessments of loss and waste.

framework.name: UN Environment Programme
framework.gloss: Reports tracking household and retail food waste.

whatYouCanDo: Plan meals and store food properly.
Support better cold chains and storage.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. Estimates of food waste carry uncertainty.

prompt: Explain how livestock and diets connect to climate.
hook: What we eat has a footprint.

card.oneLiner: Livestock produces methane and uses land and water, so shifting toward more plant-rich diets lowers emissions, even as livestock supports livelihoods.
keyPoints: Ruminants release methane during digestion.
Feed and pasture drive land use and deforestation pressure.
Plant-rich and diverse diets generally have lower footprints.
In India, dairy is also central to nutrition and livelihoods.

framework.name: FAO
framework.gloss: Assessment of emissions from livestock systems.

framework.name: IPCC AR6
framework.gloss: Mitigation options in food systems and diets.

whatYouCanDo: Add more plant proteins and seasonal vegetables.
Reduce food waste, especially of animal products.
Respect that food choices are personal and context-specific.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. Dietary advice should consider nutrition and culture.
